recognize_zh: 網狀纖維染色（reticulin stain）下，脂肪細胞間可見許多黑色細絲狀纖維，彼此分枝交錯形成疏鬆網路（尤其右側與中央），超過正常零散的纖維量；左上方另見棕色含鐵血黃素沉積。這代表輕度網狀纖維化，在 GATA2 缺乏相關的兒童骨髓衰竭／MDS 中常見。
features: Silver-impregnated reticulin fibers visible as thin black branching threads throughout the interstitium
Loose network with frequent intersections around adipocytes and between hematopoietic cells, without collagen bundles (approximately MF-1)
Patchy cellularity with numerous adipocytes; hematopoietic cells show a counterstained pink-red appearance
Golden-brown pigment clumps at upper left, consistent with hemosiderin
No coarse thick fibers or osteosclerosis in this field
describe_en: Reticulin stain of the bone marrow core biopsy shows an increased number of thin, black reticulin fibers forming a loose network with frequent intersections, particularly around adipocytes and within cellular areas. Coarse thick fibers and collagen bundles are not seen, corresponding to mild reticulin fibrosis (approximately MF-1). Hemosiderin-laden macrophages are present at the upper left. In a child with germline GATA2 mutation, monosomy 7 and hypocellular marrow, reticulin fibrosis is a supportive feature of GATA2 deficiency-associated myelodysplasia (refractory cytopenia of childhood).

ddx.vs: Normal marrow shows only scattered linear fibers without intersections, whereas this field shows a branching network with many crossings.

PMF shows dense diffuse fibers (MF-2/3) with collagen, osteosclerosis and clustered bizarre megakaryocytes in a usually hypercellular marrow, unlike the mild fibrosis in a hypocellular pediatric marrow here.
Aplastic anemia typically lacks increased reticulin; significant reticulin fibrosis in a hypocellular marrow favors hypocellular MDS/GATA2 deficiency.
